industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying a view that moved inside the industry this week: Software B2B Enterprise goes to Neutral on the rotation into software, Semiconductors stays Underweight on the AI capital spending re-pricing, Hardware stays Neutral with the evidence moved against it at the margin. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the market has stopped paying for AI capital spending (hyperscaler prints gave no lift, ABB sold on data-centre orders) while demand is intact and sub-sector upgrades continue (memory, equipment, power electronics), and the software-against-semiconductors factor pair is reversing (Goldman Sachs' desk, 26 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, B prior. The industry row stays C because the industry is split by the rotation itself. Counter-case for D: the Nasdaq down 6% in two weeks with momentum down 15% is a regime statement about this industry; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Underweight, carried, with one of its two conditions for Neutral now met and the sector's sub-sector news positive while the industry de-rates. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the market stopped paying for AI capital spending (Microsoft $11 billion below consensus, Alphabet unchanged, 'no incremental help' for semiconductors, Jefferies 29 October; Lam, Applied Materials, Teradyne and KLA down 21 to 25% in two weeks with only 22% of names oversold and the washout 'not complete'), and data-centre debt markets are 'almost entirely shut off' for borrowers without independent revenue, so the AI-credit condition is not met; against it Jefferies' European team expects the sector to 'trade up nicely' on SK Hynix's sold-out memory and ASM International's 2027 guide 5% above consensus, Aixtron's power electronics orders are turning, and Europe's exposure is equipment, power and optics, so the sell-side-call condition is met. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, A prior, the market still ranks the sector near the top while cutting its multiple. Ten Pool names, ASML at the Bench cut (rank 17) and leaving the Pool. Counter-case: demand was never the problem and a D on ten Pool names pushes the Lists away from the one European industry with upgrades; the sub-sector upgrades are stock-by-stock reasons, not a row reason. To C when the AI credit channel stabilises or a second house joins the European call with relative strength holding B.

geography.why: Double Underweight, carried. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the French ten-year premium reached a record 150 basis points, 'a lot for a core European country' (Pacific, 26 October), the 2027 deficit is seen at 5.4% of output (Goldman Sachs, 25 October), euro-exposed assets underperformed their global betas because of France (GOAL, 26 October), 2027's 300 billion of issuance makes this 'just the warmup' and the election in May or June 2027 is the earliest point anything changes; against it, Moody's affirmation removed a sovereign tail risk (DNB Carnegie, 26 October) and the French Hidden Champions newsletter sees institutional outflows from French small and mid caps as a contrarian set-up. Ten Pool names, TotalEnergies at rank 24 near the Bench cut with a global revenue base the row does not describe well. Counter-case: the affirmation and the contrarian set-up. To D on the premium under 120 basis points for a month; back to C under 100.
